title: How to Install Window Tint Without Removing the Window Trim on a Porsche 911 Targa
description: A footage-backed walkthrough of tinting the Porsche 911 Targa rear window while leaving the surrounding trim and plastics assembled. The installer explains the access constraints, careful cleaning, wet application, and squeegee direction used around the tight glass.

sections.title: Set up the rear window without removing trim
sections.text: The video opens in the back of a Target with the Targa convertible top raised. The installer says he will tint the rear window without taking apart the surrounding plastics, because unnecessary disassembly creates liability on an expensive car. He also explains that the work area has to stay clean while the film is worked behind the trim. Early preparation includes wiping the plastic, avoiding wetting it, and keeping shoes and tools from dragging dirt through the interior.

sections.title: Clean every part of the glass
sections.text: The cleaning section is unusually specific. The installer uses a scrubber to remove contamination and says the back-window defrost lines are inside the glass, so a razor should not be used on the surface. He works across the entire pane and repeats the cleaning because one avoidable speck can mean redoing the window. He then wipes the surrounding plastics again, keeping them clean and dry before the film is handled.

sections.title: Form and roll the film for the tight access
sections.text: After trimming and wetting the film, the installer describes a back roll, also called a California roll, as a way to make this installation more manageable. He keeps spraying as the film is lifted so exposed adhesive is not left dry, then smooths large air pockets while the film is still on the strongly curved glass. The liner is rolled tightly and continuously on the pane; he notes that a loose start makes the rest of the roll want to come apart. Personal preferences, such as which side to start from and how to orient the film, are clearly identified as preferences rather than universal rules.

sections.title: Unroll carefully and manage tension
sections.text: Inside the car, the installer sprays slip solution along the upper edge and corners, explaining that gel can catch dirt so it can be pushed out. He unrolls from his preferred side while supporting the film on his arm and warns that one wrong move can crease it. As the film comes down, he keeps adding slip, pulls the liner gradually and lets the film float rather than forcing it dry. He points out that plotter patterns can be slightly large and that a helper can check for light gaps while the film is still movable.

sections.title: Anchor the center, then work the curves
sections.text: The main squeegee work starts in the middle and moves outward, pushing tension and air pockets toward the edges. The installer creates an anchor point, works toward the curve, and revisits sections two or three times before they dry. He says efficiency matters because drying solution can leave ghosting marks. For stubborn fingers that keep returning, he changes direction, uses a firmer two-handed squeegee, wraps a tool in a towel when needed, and works the curved area repeatedly until the water is out.

sections.title: Heat-set the final fingers and inspect
sections.text: Near the end, the installer uses a flexible plastic tool for hard-to-reach areas and a heat gun to help settle remaining fingers. He says to keep the heat directed away from the trim and uses a short, roughly five-second application as an example, with the practical check that the glass should not be too hot to touch. He acknowledges that a small speck can occur on a difficult back window and continues inspecting the edges and lower glass before closing the walkthrough.

title: How to Install PPF for Porsche 997 Carrera Front Fender
description: A detailed installation walkthrough for applying XPEL Ultimate Plus paint protection film to the front fender of a 2012 Porsche 997 Carrera. The footage follows wetting, positioning, stretching, edge management, and finishing passes on the fender.

sections.title: Prepare the 997 and keep the adhesive clean
sections.text: The installer begins by explaining that the adhesive side should not be touched because small particles from fingers can end up under the film. He wets the fender and discusses the 2012 997's removable headlight mechanism: a carpet section and water seal are moved, then a 5 mm socket is used to release the light. That access detail is specific to the car shown, and he contrasts it with the later 991 design. He grabs the film from the side that will wrap under the hood and watches the nearby tire while carrying it into position.

sections.title: Tack the pattern and control the stretch
sections.text: The video uses a mixture described as roughly 10% alcohol with the rest water to tack the initial edge. The installer explains that he starts at the back on this 997, while a different pattern may lead him to start at the front. He leaves a small edge allowance, works backward and uses a snow-plow motion to move solution. The cloth matters because it lets him check that nothing is trapped under the film before locking the next section. He keeps his hands on the outside where possible and checks for the edge before each move.

sections.title: Lift only the section you can clean
sections.text: When a concave area needs more work, he lifts the film from a portion that can be trimmed later, sprays soap under it and massages the solution around the end of the wet line. He warns against pushing soap or alcohol into an already locked area because it can create a hard adhesive line. The fender is divided into sections so he can inspect for a bubble or contaminant before it becomes trapped. A small speck slows the job, so he washes the area, checks it again and uses alcohol only where he wants the edge to stay.

sections.title: Work fingers into smaller, controllable paths
sections.text: The installer calls out an existing scratch on the 30,000-mile car so it is not mistaken for an installation defect. When a large finger forms, he starts farther back, breaks it into smaller fingers with a shovel motion, adds a little alcohol and leaves an escape path for water and solution. He avoids locking a pocket in place. He also explains that the material should sit slightly beyond the edge and be trimmed after it has dried rather than being pulled while wet. The dry microfiber check helps reveal streaks and the actual edge condition.

sections.title: Let the film cure, then finish the edges
sections.text: The installer says the PPF takes about a month to fully cure and describes asking customers to return for a later inspection. He notes that warmth and sun can help fluid leave the film, while cold conditions make installation and drying less forgiving. Later, he applies a small amount of an XPEL edge-prep product to edges, cautioning that it should not go on plastic and that carbon surfaces require particular care. The final edge pass is compared to edging a lawn: let the area dry, use alcohol carefully, re-squeegee the line and remove remaining pockets. He waits to trim fully until the film is drier so the edge does not lift.

title: 2024 INEOS Grenadier Window Tint and Paint Protection
service: Paint protection film and window tint
description: A short finished-vehicle walkthrough of a 2024 INEOS Grenadier after front and side paint protection film plus window tint. The presenter identifies the protected panels, the darker rear tint, and the clear 70% film used on the front windows.

sections.title: Front and side protection
sections.text: The presenter says the Grenadier received full front PPF on the fenders and hood, plus half doors down the sides, A-pillars, and the roof edge. He describes the result as cleanly finished.

sections.title: Tint balanced for privacy
sections.text: The walkaround identifies XPEL XR Plus Prime tint, with a darker shade on the rear windows for privacy. The front windows use clear 70% film.

sections.title: Finished vehicle walkaround
sections.text: The closing footage circles the completed Grenadier outside the shop, giving a direct visual check of the protected front end, side coverage, and tinted glass.
